chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Aslam, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)
performed phlebotomy on a Wednesday while he had a fever. The fever did not leave him, so he performed phlebotomy on Friday, and the fever left him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (Imam al-Kadhim)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Musa al-Kadhim's phlebotomy on Wednesday and Friday?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the practical application of the Sunnah of cupping (hijama) by Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), linking specific days of the week to therapeutic efficacy. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining spiritual devotion with physical health practices, as recorded by early hadith compilers like al-Saduq to preserve the Imams' daily habits.
